newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says state firms dabbling more in crime.
newsitem.headline: Russia says state firms dabbling more in crime.

text.p: Directors of Russia's state-owned enterprises are increasingly becoming involved with the criminal underworld, the government's top crimefighter said on Friday.

"In the criminal world there is a a growing tendency to draw directors of government enterprises into cooperation," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Kulikov as telling parliament. Kulikov is also Interior Minister.

Because the directors of state enterprises were in control of many key spheres of the economy when the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, many were in a position to become rich quickly -- often outside the bounds of the law.

Kulikov, who was promoted to deputy premier this month with a brief to fight economic crime, said state firms' involvement came during a period of transition among Russian crime bosses, following the arrests and deaths of several "godfathers".
He said his ministry had also recently sent regional police orders to step up the fight against criminal bosses.
